content.overview: Every Producer Company shall have at least five and not more than fifteen directors. In the case of an inter-State co-operative society incorporated as a Producer Company, such company may have more than fifteen directors for a period of one year from the date of its incorporation as a Producer Company.
content.glance: Board size is 5–15 directors; converted inter-State co-operatives may exceed 15 for one year.
content.study: Section 378O fixes the minimum and maximum number of directors of a Producer Company. The ordinary range is five to fifteen. A converted inter-State co-operative society may retain more than fifteen directors for one year from incorporation as a Producer Company, after which the ordinary ceiling applies.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: A Producer Company must have at least five and not more than fifteen directors, subject to a one-year higher ceiling for converted inter-State co-operative societies.

examples.title: Illustration — s. 378O
examples.body: A newly formed Producer Company with seven directors complies with the 5–15 range in s. 378O.

hypotheticals.question: What is the core effect of s. 378O?
hypotheticals.analysis: It fixes the board-size range at 5–15, with a one-year transitional higher ceiling for converted inter-State co-operative societies.

rows.right: Appointment of directors (s. 378P) or continuity of directors on conversion (s. 378N)

misconceptions.trap: Applying the ordinary s. 149 board-size rules without regard to this Part.
misconceptions.correction: Producer Company board size is governed by s. 378O, not the general s. 149 minima/maxima.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should s. 378O be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. State the 5–15 range. II. Note the one-year higher ceiling for converted inter-State co-operatives. III. Conclude.

revisionPoints: Number of directors — at least 5, not more than 15 (with 1-year transitional exception)
